title: GADT variant results and package roles are not implemented: GADT results and package roles get generic diagnostics
Embedding simplification cannot be fully exercised: the prototype compiles one module without trait imports, so trait availability is untested, and the fixtures need package roles
Visibility-aware member lookup cannot be exercised: the prototype compiles one module, so every own member is visible, and the fixtures need package roles
The trait-argument ownership fixture for a foreign trait argument needs package roles, which the prototype lacks
Typed derivation M29's per-trait Self-line warning needs a second package, and the prototype CLI has no package roles
The `disposed-file` runtime profile named in spec/conformance/README.md does not exist
An initialization group's statements are not interleaved: the package linker joins the group's modules by identity, so a read of a later-joined module's binding fails
A script's top-level println needs the inferred script entry requirement row, which the prototype does not infer

Generic call inference from several arguments (batch 17, INF-mut) is not implemented: an i32 and an i64 argument widen instead of type-mismatch, a User and a Display argument are type-mismatch instead of no-common-type, and assert_equal still coerces expected to the type of actual

Explicit type arguments in expressions take `::` (batch 22, D1 and D3): the prototype does not parse `::[`, still accepts a type name's arguments without `::`, and reads brackets before `(` as type arguments
Callable values (D1 callable-value part, D2, D4): the prototype does not know `Apply` or `Update`, so `v() = x` is invalid-assignment-target and `impl Apply` is unknown-trait
Iterator is not Iterable (batch 24, IT2): lib/std/iter.hd still implements Iterable for Iterator, so the prototype accepts an iterator for an Iterable bound
A template's qualified Structure:: call (batch 25, ST8-self): the prototype resolves a receiverless template call only as T::name() or T::facts(), so Structure::name() is unknown-type
Bang calls in comprehensions (batch 26, Syntax And Semantics Cost Q2): the prototype still rejects every bang call in a comprehension as suspension-forbidden-context
One dollar rule for every string (batch 26, Q3): the prototype lexer still rejects a plain-string $ that begins no interpolation
Parenthesized for lists (batch 26, Q4): the prototype parses only a bare name list after for, so for (key, value) in m is a syntax-error and the bare form is accepted
Multi-name bindings are statements (batch 26, Q5): the prototype accepts ((a, b) := value) and reports the withdrawn multi-binding-needs-parentheses for [(a, b) := value]
Map keys through the declared bound (batch 26, Q7): the prototype reports invalid-map-key for a missing Eq or Hash, and accepts a mut key type
Map index reads V (batch 26, Q8): the prototype still types m[k] as V?
Generic derived Arbitrary (batch 26, AT-gen): the prototype's checker-generated Arbitrary gives a member's type parameter no Inspectable bound

Patterns in let (batch 26, LP1 and LP1-one): the prototype's let takes only a name or a parenthesized name list and has no let-else, so data, variant, and nested patterns are syntax-error; it still accepts a multi-name := and reports other patterns before := as syntax-error, not missing-let
List items may be bindings (batch 26, Q5-list): the prototype reports the withdrawn multi-binding-needs-parentheses for [a, b := value]
Tuples have no mut form (batch 27, TU2): the prototype accepts a mut tuple parameter type and reports mutable-upgrade, not mut-on-tuple, for a mut tuple annotation and for let mut on a tuple
A template's call qualified by the derived trait (batch 28, ST8-own): the prototype reports Named::name() as associated-function-needs-target
The retry! library loop (batch 29, RETRY): the prototype has no std.task.retry
Patterns in for (batch 30, LP-for): the prototype's for and comprehension for take only a name or a bare name list, so a data pattern and a refutable pattern are syntax-error
An else after an irrefutable let pattern (batch 30, LP-irrefutable-else): the prototype's let has no else block, so it is syntax-error, not unreachable-match-arm
let _ discards a must-use value (batch 30, LP-discard): the prototype's let takes no _ pattern, so let _ = save() is syntax-error
Tuple elements may be bindings (batch 30, Q5-tuple): the prototype still rejects (a, b := value) as the withdrawn grouped binding
Varargs belong to the declaration (batch 31, VARARG-SPELL): the prototype keeps the vararg in a function value's type and accepts fn(i32...) -> i32
Tuple-typed varargs (batch 31, VARARG-TYPE): the prototype supports only a List[T] vararg, so a tuple or Tuple-bounded vararg is unsupported-tuple-vararg
The Tuple marker trait (batch 31, Q5): the prototype has no std.function.Tuple and makes Fn inputs tuple-kinded only by use
Tuple spread (batch 31, Q8): a spread still needs a vararg, so a tuple spread into fixed parameters is positional-spread-needs-vararg
The plain race! signature (batch 31, Q7): the prototype reports every race! call as unsupported-task-combinator
Packs are removed in the specification, but the prototype still parses type packs, pack expansion, and pack.map(, and has no std.function.Tuple
all! has one typing rule, but the prototype reports every all! call as unsupported-task-combinator
Tuples derive Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, and Hash, but the prototype has no Eq or Hash for tuples, so a tuple map key is invalid-map-key
A reserved word is never a suffix (batch 31, Q1 cut C3): the prototype still lexes 5else as a suffixed literal and reports invalid-token, not syntax-error
-5s is the ordinary negation -(5s) (batch 31, Q3): the prototype folds the minus into the literal, as s(-5), so it needs no Neg and range-checks the negated value
